functions.name: ijlInit
functions.comment:
Initializes a JPEG_CORE_PROPERTIES structure for Intel JPEG Library operations.

Algorithm:
1. Set up SEH exception handling frame
2. Initialize JFIF interchange format structure at offset 0x58 with defaults
3. Zero-initialize core property fields (image dimensions, color space, subsampling)
4. Set default subsampling to 4:2:0 mode (values 3 and 2 for H/V factors)
5. Configure default quality factor to 75 (0x4B)
6. Initialize 4 component scan parameter slots via loop (offsets 0x36E4-0x3704)
7. Align 4 component data pointers to 8-byte boundaries via loop
8. Allocate 64 bytes for quantization tables via operator_new
9. Return IJL_MEMORY_ERROR (-5) if allocation fails
10. Zero-initialize 4 quantization table slots (16 bytes each)
11. Initialize Huffman codec state flags (offset 0x37DC)
12. Zero-initialize extended codec state fields (offsets 0x37A4-0x4834)
13. Call InitJpegProcessorDefaults to configure Huffman and quantization tables
14. Detect CPU capabilities via FUN_60017eb0 and store result
15. Initialize additional processor state fields (offsets 0x4DD8-0x4DE4)
16. Return IJL_OK (0) on success

Parameters:
    pProps (JPEG_CORE_PROPERTIES*) - Pointer to JPEG_CORE_PROPERTIES structure (minimum 0x4DE8 bytes)

Returns:
    int - IJL_OK (0) on success, IJL_MEMORY_ERROR (-5) if memory allocation fails

Structure Layout (JPEG_CORE_PROPERTIES):
    Offset   Size  Field                Description
    0x0000   4     dwReserved           Reserved field
    0x0004   4     dwWidth              Image width
    0x0008   4     dwHeight             Image height  
    0x000C   4     dwChannels           Number of color channels
    0x0010   4     dwBitsPerChannel     Bits per channel
    0x0014   4     dwSubsampH           Horizontal subsampling (3=4:1:1, 2=4:2:2)
    0x0018   4     dwSubsampV           Vertical subsampling (2=4:2:0)
    0x001C   4     dwColorSpace         Color space identifier
    0x0048   4     dwQualityFactor      JPEG quality 1-100 (default 75)
    0x004C   4     dwRestartInterval    Restart marker interval
    0x0050   4     dwJpegSize           JPEG data size in bytes
    0x0058   128   jfifHeader           JFIF interchange format structure
    0x37CC   4     pQuantTables         Pointer to allocated quantization tables
    0x381C   4     dwCpuCapabilities    CPU feature flags from detection

Magic Numbers:
    0x03 - Default horizontal subsampling factor (4:1:1 mode)
    0x02 - Default vertical subsampling factor (4:2:0 mode)
    0x01 - Progressive scan mode enabled
    0x4B - Default JPEG quality factor (75 decimal)
    0x40 - Quantization table allocation size (64 bytes)
    -0x05 - IJL_MEMORY_ERROR return code

Error Handling:
    Returns -5 (IJL_MEMORY_ERROR) if operator_new fails to allocate quantization tables.
    SEH frame installed for exception safety during initialization.

functions.name: ijlFree
functions.comment:
Releases all resources associated with an Intel JPEG Library (IJL) structure.

Algorithm:
1. Close any open file handle at offset +0x387C of internal structure
2. Validate state counter at offset +0x3818 is <= 255 (0xFF)
3. Free scan line buffer at offset +0x3824
4. Free DIB data buffer at offset +0x4E3C
5. Free 4 channel buffers in array at offset +0x373C (loop i=0..3)
6. Free thumbnail buffer at offset +0x4888
7. Free sub-structure at offset +0x3838 and its nested buffer at +0x34
8. Clear dimension fields (width, height, etc.) at offsets +0x80 to +0x8C

Parameters:
    pJpegProps (JPEG_CORE_PROPERTIES*): Pointer to IJL JPEG properties structure

Returns:
    int: IJL error code
        0 (IJL_OK) - Success, all resources freed
        -9 (IJL_ERR_FILE_CLOSE) - Failed to close file handle
        -8 (IJL_ERR_DATA) - Invalid state (counter > 255)

Error Handling:
    Uses SEH exception handling with scope table at g_adwIjlFreeSehScopeTable
    All free operations check for NULL before calling AtoiMbcsWrapper (free)

Magic Numbers:
    0xFF (255) - Maximum valid state counter value
    0x58 - Offset from JPEG_CORE_PROPERTIES to internal state structure
    0x3824 - File handle offset
    0x37C0 - State counter offset
    0x37CC - Scan line buffer offset
    0x4DE4 - DIB data buffer offset
    0x36E4 - Channel buffer array base offset
    0x4830 - Thumbnail buffer offset
    0x37E0 - Sub-structure pointer offset

functions.name: ijlRead
functions.comment:
Reads and parses JPEG image data from file or memory buffer.

This is the main entry point for Intel JPEG Library read operations. It validates
parameters, opens files if needed, copies user settings to internal state, parses
JPEG markers, and determines the subsampling mode of the image.

Algorithm:
1. Set up SEH exception frame for error recovery
2. Store I/O type in internal state at offset 0x58
3. Call ValidateJpegParams to validate JPEG_CORE_PROPERTIES structure
4. Set read flag for header-only operations (IoTypes 0,1,4,5,0x14,0x15)
5. Clear dimension fields for non-continuing read operations
6. Open file if file-based I/O and handle not already open
7. Copy user buffer settings to internal state when mode is 0
8. Initialize internal buffer pointers based on I/O type
9. Adjust buffer pointer for negative height (bottom-up DIB)
10. Parse JPEG marker stream via ProcessJpegMarkerStream
11. On partial success, calculate actual image dimensions from MCU blocks
12. Seek back in file for file-based operations that need re-read
13. Copy parsed image properties back to output structure
14. Determine subsampling mode (0=none, 1=422, 2=422H, 3=411, 4=411H)
15. Close file handle for header-only file reads

Parameters:
  pJpegProps - Pointer to JPEG_CORE_PROPERTIES structure containing I/O settings
               and receiving parsed image properties
  nIoType    - IJLIOTYPE enumeration specifying the read operation type:
               0  = IJL_JFILE_READPARAMS (file header only)
               1  = IJL_JBUFF_READPARAMS (buffer header only)
               2  = IJL_JFILE_READHEADER (file header, close after)
               4  = IJL_JFILE_READWHOLEIMAGE (file full decode)
               6  = IJL_JFILE_READENTROPY (file entropy only)
               0x10 = IJL_JFILE_READTHUMBNAIL
               0x12 = IJL_JFILE_READTHUMBNAIL_HEADER
               0x14 = IJL_JFILE_READIMAGEC
               0x15 = IJL_JBUFF_READIMAGEC

Returns:
  0          - Success (IJL_OK)
  0xFFFFFFF6 - File open failed (IJL_FILE_NOT_FOUND, -10)
  0xFFFFFFF7 - File close failed (IJL_ERR_FILE_CLOSE, -9)
  0xFFFFFFE9 - File seek failed (IJL_ERR_FILE_SEEK, -23)
  Other      - Error code from ValidateJpegParams or ProcessJpegMarkerStream

I/O Type Constants:
  0x00 = IJL_JFILE_READPARAMS     0x01 = IJL_JBUFF_READPARAMS
  0x02 = IJL_JFILE_READHEADER     0x03 = IJL_JBUFF_READHEADER  
  0x04 = IJL_JFILE_READWHOLEIMAGE 0x05 = IJL_JBUFF_READWHOLEIMAGE
  0x06 = IJL_JFILE_READENTROPY    0x07 = IJL_JBUFF_READENTROPY
  0x10 = IJL_JFILE_READTHUMBNAIL  0x11 = IJL_JBUFF_READTHUMBNAIL
  0x14 = IJL_JFILE_READIMAGEC     0x15 = IJL_JBUFF_READIMAGEC

Subsampling Mode Output (offset 0x3C):
  0x00 = No subsampling (1:1:1)
  0x01 = 4:2:2 horizontal
  0x02 = 4:2:2 vertical  
  0x03 = 4:1:1 CMYK horizontal
  0x04 = 4:1:1 CMYK vertical
  0xFF = Unknown/unsupported

Structure Layout (JPEG_CORE_PROPERTIES internal offsets used):
  0x00     Mode (0=user buffer, else internal)
  0x04-1C  User DIB settings (copied to 0x78+)
  0x20     File path string pointer
  0x58     I/O type storage (pnIoState)
  0x3834   Read operation flag
  0x387C   File handle storage

functions.name: ijlWrite
functions.comment:
Intel JPEG Library write function - encodes and writes JPEG image data.

Algorithm:
1. Setup SEH exception frame for error handling
2. Store I/O mode in JPEG properties structure at offset 0x58
3. Validate JPEG parameters via ValidateJpegParams
4. If file-based write modes (8, 10, 12) and no file handle, open output file with GENERIC_READ|GENERIC_WRITE
5. If initial state, copy DIB parameters to JPEG core state (dimensions, padding, color format)
6. Calculate stride and handle negative heights for bottom-up DIBs
7. Allocate component sampling table if channel count changed (16 bytes per channel)
8. Configure subsampling factors based on JPG_SUBSAMPLING mode (0-4):
   - Case 0: No subsampling (1:1:1)
   - Case 1: 4:2:2 horizontal subsampling
   - Case 2: 4:2:2 vertical subsampling
   - Case 3/4: 4:2:0 subsampling (2x2 chroma)
9. Calculate MCU dimensions and block counts based on max sampling factors
10. If not file-based mode, write JPEG headers via FUN_60017980
11. Encode image data via ProcessJpegEncodeScan
12. For progressive writes (mode 1/2), update progress counters
13. Close file handle if opened and return status

Parameters:
pnJpegProps (int*): Pointer to JPEG_CORE_PROPERTIES structure containing:
  - [0x00]: dwIOType - I/O type (0=memory, 1=file)
  - [0x08]: lpszFileName - Output file path for file modes
  - [0x0d]: nChannels - Number of color channels
  - [0x0f]: eSubsampling - JPG_SUBSAMPLING enumeration
  - [0x12]: nQuality - JPEG quality factor (0-100)
  - [0x58]: nIOMode - Current operation mode
  - [0x3824]: hFile - File handle for file I/O
  - [0x37cc]: pComponentInfo - Per-component sampling info

nIoMode (int): JPEG I/O operation mode:
  - 8: IJL_JFILE_WRITEWHOLEIMAGE
  - 9: IJL_JBUFF_WRITEWHOLEIMAGE
  - 10: IJL_JFILE_WRITEHEADER
  - 11: IJL_JBUFF_WRITEHEADER
  - 12: IJL_JFILE_WRITEENTROPY
  - 13: IJL_JBUFF_WRITEENTROPY

Returns:
0 (IJL_OK): Success
0xFFFFFFF6 (-10): IJL_FILE_ERROR - Failed to open output file
0xFFFFFFF7 (-9): IJL_FILE_ERROR - Failed to close file
0xFFFFFFFB (-5): IJL_MEMORY_ERROR - Component buffer allocation failed
Other: Validation error from ValidateJpegParams

Error Handling:
- Uses SEH for exception safety
- Restores exception list on all exit paths
- Returns specific error codes for file and memory failures

functions.name: ijlErrorStr
functions.comment:
Converts an Intel JPEG Library (IJL) error code to a human-readable error string.

Algorithm:
1. Adjust error code by adding 0x63 (99) to normalize the range
2. If adjusted value exceeds 0x65 (101), return "Unknown error code"
3. Use jump table lookup via byte index table at 0x6001a160
4. Jump to appropriate case handler via jump table at 0x6001a0e0
5. Return pointer to static error message string

Parameters:
  nErrorCode (int) - IJL error code value (typically negative for errors, 0 for success)

Returns:
  char* - Pointer to static null-terminated error message string

Error Code Mapping (partial):
  0 (IJL_OK)                    -> "Success"
  -1 (IJL_RESERVED)             -> "Reserved"
  -2 (IJL_ERR_DATA)             -> "Data error"
  -3 (IJL_ERR_FILE)             -> "File error"
  Unrecognized codes            -> "Unknown error code"

Special Cases:
- All returned strings are statically allocated (do not free)
- Error codes use Intel JPEG Library enumeration values
- Jump table implementation for O(1) lookup performance

Magic Numbers Reference:
  0x63 (99)       - Base offset to normalize error codes
  0x65 (101)      - Maximum valid adjusted error code
  0x6001a160      - Byte index table for jump table dispatch
  0x6001a0e0      - Jump table with case handler addresses

functions.name: ValidateBinkInstallLocation
functions.comment:
Validates Bink DLL installation and dispatches initialization based on reason code.

Algorithm:
1. Check if dwReason is within valid range (0-3)
2. If dwReason > 3, return 0 (failure)
3. Use jump table to dispatch based on dwReason:
   - Case 0: Return 1 (success)
   - Case 1: Call InitializeDecoderByCapability with hModule
   - Case 2: Return 1 (success)
   - Case 3: Return 1 (success)

Parameters:
  hModule (HMODULE): Handle to the Bink DLL module being validated
  dwReason (dword): Reason code for the validation call (DLL_PROCESS_ATTACH, etc.)
    0 = DLL_PROCESS_DETACH
    1 = DLL_PROCESS_ATTACH
    2 = DLL_THREAD_ATTACH
    3 = DLL_THREAD_DETACH

Returns:
  1 (TRUE): Validation successful or no action needed
  0 (FALSE): Invalid reason code (dwReason > 3)

Special Cases:
  Only DLL_PROCESS_ATTACH (reason 1) triggers decoder initialization
  All other valid reasons are no-ops returning success

Structure Layout:
  Jump Table at 0x6001a1fc:
  Offset  Target      Case
  0x00    0x6001a1f2  Case 0 (return 1)
  0x04    0x6001a1e2  Case 1 (call InitializeDecoderByCapability)
  0x08    0x6001a1f2  Case 2 (return 1)
  0x0C    0x6001a1f2  Case 3 (return 1)

functions.name: OutputDebugStringLines
functions.comment:
Outputs a multi-line debug string with thread ID prefixes.

Algorithm:
1. Check if input string is non-empty, return immediately if empty
2. If nMaxLines > 0, initialize line buffer with 0xFF padding and space-fill
3. Get current thread ID and format prefix string "[%02X] "
4. Loop through input string, splitting on newline (0x0A) characters
5. For each line segment, copy to buffer and null-terminate
6. If continuation line and flag bit 1 set, output thread prefix first
7. Output the line buffer via function pointer (OutputDebugString)
8. Advance to next line and repeat until end of string

Parameters:
  lpszInputString - Pointer to null-terminated input string (may contain newlines)
  nMaxLines - Maximum number of lines to format (controls buffer size)

Returns:
  void

Special Cases:
  - Empty input string returns immediately
  - Single newline character (length 1) uses alternate buffer
  - Newline detection tracks state in g_fHasNewline global

Magic Numbers Reference:
  0x0A (10) - ASCII newline character
  0xFF (-1) - Buffer initialization fill value
  0x20 (' ') - Space padding character
  0x02 - Flag bit in g_dwDebugOutputFlags for prefix output

Structure Layout:
  Offset   Size   Field             Description
  0x000    512    szLineBuffer      Formatted line output buffer
  0x200    12     szThreadPrefix    Thread ID prefix "[XX] "

functions.name: FUN_6001a420
strings:
0x27280|s_Assertion_failed_in_%s(%d)_Reaso_60027280|Assertion failed in %s(%d)
Reason: %s
Module: %s

(Press "Retry" to debug the application)

functions.name: ShowMessageBoxPreserveQuit
functions.signature: int ShowMessageBoxPreserveQuit(LPCSTR lpszText, UINT dwType, uint dwReserved, LPCSTR lpszCaption)
functions.comment:
Displays a message box while preserving any pending WM_QUIT messages.

This function safely shows a MessageBox without losing WM_QUIT messages that may have been
posted before the dialog appeared. Modal dialogs can consume quit messages, so this wrapper
peeks for WM_QUIT first, shows the dialog, then re-posts the quit if one was pending.

Algorithm:
1. Peek for WM_QUIT (0x12) message in the queue, removing it if found
2. Display the MessageBox with the provided text, caption, and type
3. If a WM_QUIT was found in step 1, re-post it with the original wParam (exit code)
4. Return the MessageBox result

Parameters:
  lpszText - Message text to display in the dialog body
  dwType - MessageBox type flags (MB_OK, MB_YESNO, etc.)
  dwReserved - Unused parameter (reserved for future use)
  lpszCaption - Caption/title text for the dialog window

Returns:
  int - MessageBox return value (IDOK, IDYES, IDNO, IDCANCEL, etc.)

Special Cases:
  - If WM_QUIT was pending, it will be re-posted after dialog closes
  - The wParam from the original WM_QUIT is preserved (exit code)

Magic Numbers:
  0x12 - WM_QUIT message identifier
  0x1 - PM_REMOVE flag for PeekMessageA (removes message from queue)

functions.name: BinkBufferGetError
functions.comment:
Retrieves pointer to the global Bink buffer error message string.

Algorithm:
1. Return address of global error buffer array g_szErrorBuffer

Parameters:
None

Returns:
char * - Pointer to null-terminated error message string in g_szErrorBuffer
         The buffer contains the most recent error message from Bink buffer operations
         Returns valid pointer to 256-byte character array (never NULL)

Special Cases:
- Function always returns same buffer address (0x1002f01c)
- Error buffer is shared across all Bink buffer operations
- Calling code should copy error message if persistence needed
- Buffer content may be overwritten by subsequent Bink operations

Magic Numbers Reference:
0x1002f01c - Address of global error buffer g_szErrorBuffer (256 bytes)

functions.name: InitModuleVersionInfo
functions.comment:
Initializes module version information from PE version resource.

Extracts version data from the specified module's embedded version resource
and stores it in global variables for later access.

Algorithm:
1. Get module file path using GetModuleFileNameA
2. Query version info size using GetFileVersionInfoSizeA
3. Allocate buffer and retrieve version info using GetFileVersionInfoA
4. Query VS_FIXEDFILEINFO root block for file version numbers
5. Extract major.minor.build.revision from dwFileVersionMS/LS
6. Query ProductVersion and OriginalFileName strings
7. Format version string as "[major.minor.build.revision]"
8. Store pointers to version strings in global table

Parameters:
  hModule - Handle to module to extract version info from (HMODULE)

Returns:
  BOOL - TRUE if version info extracted successfully, FALSE on failure

Special Cases:
  - Returns FALSE if module path cannot be retrieved
  - Returns FALSE if no version resource exists
  - Returns FALSE if memory allocation fails
  - Returns FALSE if version queries fail

Globals Modified:
  g_dwVersionMajor   - Major version number (HIWORD of dwFileVersionMS)
  g_dwVersionMinor   - Minor version number (LOWORD of dwFileVersionMS)
  g_dwVersionBuild   - Build number (HIWORD of dwFileVersionLS)
  g_szProductVersion - Product version string buffer
  g_szOriginalFilename - Original filename string buffer
  g_szVersionString  - Formatted version "[x.x.x.x]" buffer
  g_pszOriginalFilename - Pointer to g_szOriginalFilename
  g_pszProductVersion - Pointer to g_szProductVersion
  g_pszVersionString - Pointer to g_szVersionString
  g_pszBuildDate     - Pointer to build date string
  g_pszModuleType    - Pointer to module type "DLL"

functions.name: ReadBytesFromJpegStream
functions.signature: int ReadBytesFromJpegStream(uint * pStreamCtx, uint dwBytesRequested, byte * * ppbAllocatedBuffer, byte * * ppbDataOut, int * pnBufferAllocated)
functions.comment:
Reads bytes from JPEG stream context with automatic buffer allocation.

Algorithm:
1. Check if requested bytes exceed available buffer (pStreamCtx+0x24)
2. If within buffer: call FUN_600010a0 to get pointer directly from stream
3. If exceeds buffer: allocate new buffer via operator_new
4. Copy available bytes from stream buffer using g_pfnMemcpy
5. Loop reading remaining bytes in 0x1000 (4096) byte chunks
6. Handle read errors by freeing allocated buffer

Parameters:
  pStreamCtx - Pointer to JPEG stream context structure
               +0x10: Current read position pointer
               +0x1c: Bytes read counter
               +0x24: Bytes remaining in buffer
  dwBytesRequested - Number of bytes to read
  ppbAllocatedBuffer - OUT: Receives allocated buffer pointer (for cleanup)
  ppbDataOut - OUT: Receives pointer to actual data
  pnBufferAllocated - OUT: Set to 1 if buffer was allocated, 0 otherwise

Returns:
  0 on success
  -5 (0xFFFFFFFB) on allocation failure
  -21 (0xFFFFFFEB) on read error (cleans up allocated buffer)
  Other error codes from FUN_600010a0

Magic Numbers:
  0x1000 - Chunk size for multi-read operations (4KB)
  0xFFFF - Maximum single read size check

Note: pbWritePtr is decompiler-generated (undefined1 *) and cannot be explicitly typed via API.

functions.name: ReadNextJpegMarkerCode
functions.comment:
Reads the next JPEG marker code from a stream context.

Algorithm:
1. Check if cached marker byte exists at context+0x30
2. If cached, clear cache, normalize marker, output to pdwMarkerCode, return success
3. Otherwise, skip entropy-coded data to find next 0xFF marker
4. If skip failed (EOF), propagate error code
5. Read one byte from stream for marker code
6. If read failed, output 0x100 (invalid marker) as fallback, return success
7. Normalize marker code and output to pdwMarkerCode

Parameters:
    pStreamContext - Pointer to JPEG stream context structure
    pdwMarkerCode - Output pointer for normalized marker code

Returns:
    0 on success (marker code written to pdwMarkerCode)
    Non-zero error code on stream failure

Special Cases:
    - Cached byte at offset 0x30 provides look-ahead for marker parsing
    - RST markers (0xD0-0xDF) are normalized to 0xD0 by FUN_6001a750
    - If read fails after skip, outputs 0x100 as invalid marker sentinel

Structure Layout (pStreamContext):
    Offset  Size  Field       Description
    0x10    4     pBuffer     Current read position
    0x18    4     dwBufEnd    Buffer end position  
    0x1C    4     dwBytesRead Total bytes consumed
    0x24    4     dwBufAvail  Bytes available in buffer
    0x30    1     bCachedByte Cached marker byte (look-ahead)
    0x3C    4     pRefillFunc Buffer refill callback

functions.name: SkipJpegMarkerSegment
functions.comment:
Skips past an unknown or unhandled JPEG marker segment in the stream.

Algorithm:
1. Read 2-byte big-endian segment length via FUN_6001aa60
2. Subtract 2 from length (length field itself is included in count)
3. If length < 2, return error -21 (invalid segment length)
4. Skip initial buffered data (from offset 0x24 of frame info)
5. Loop to skip remaining bytes in 4KB (0x1000) chunks
6. Return 0 on success

Parameters:
pFrameInfo - Pointer to JPEG frame info structure containing:
  - Offset 0x24: Current buffer size (bytes available to skip)

Returns:
0 - Success (segment fully skipped)
-21 (0xFFFFFFEB) - Invalid segment length (less than 2 bytes)
Propagates errors from FUN_6001aa60 and FUN_600010a0

Magic Numbers:
0x1000 (4096) - Maximum bytes to skip per iteration (4KB chunk)
0xFFFF (65535) - Maximum valid segment length
0x2 - Minimum valid segment length (length field itself)

functions.name: ReadBigEndian16FromJpegStream
functions.comment:
Reads a 16-bit big-endian value from a JPEG stream.

Algorithm:
1. Initialize error flag to 0
2. Call ReadBytesFromJpegStream to read 2 bytes into temporary buffer
3. If read succeeds (return 0):
   a. Extract first byte, shift left 8 bits (high byte)
   b. Extract second byte (low byte)
   c. Combine as (highByte << 8) + lowByte for big-endian value
   d. Store result in output pointer
4. Cleanup: If error flag set and temp buffer allocated, call AtoiMbcsWrapper
5. Return the result code from ReadBytesFromJpegStream

Parameters:
  pJpegStream - Pointer to JPEG stream context structure
  pnOutValue - Output pointer to receive the 16-bit value as int

Returns:
  0 on success, non-zero error code on failure

Special Cases:
  - Big-endian byte order (network/JPEG standard order)
  - Reads exactly 2 bytes for 16-bit value
  - Used for reading JPEG segment lengths and marker parameters

Callers:
  ParseJpegQuantizationTables, ParseJpegFrameHeader, ParseJpegStartOfFrame,
  ParseDhtMarkerSegment, SkipJpegMarkerSegment, ParseJfxxThumbnailData

functions.name: ReadBigEndian16FromJpegSegment
functions.comment:
Reads a 16-bit big-endian value from a JPEG segment's data content.

Algorithm:
1. Initialize output value to 0 and local buffer tracking variables
2. Call FUN_6001aa60 to read the 2-byte segment length (big-endian)
3. Validate segment length is at least 2 bytes
4. Subtract 2 from length (JPEG segment lengths include the length field itself)
5. Read remaining segment data via ReadBytesFromJpegStream
6. Extract 16-bit big-endian value: byte[0] * 256 + byte[1]
7. Store extracted value in output parameter
8. Free allocated buffer if one was created

Parameters:
  pStreamCtx - Pointer to JPEG stream context structure
  pnValueOut - OUT: Receives the extracted 16-bit big-endian value

Returns:
  0 on success
  -21 (0xFFFFFFEB) if segment length < 2 bytes (invalid segment)
  Other error codes from FUN_6001aa60 or ReadBytesFromJpegStream

Magic Numbers:
  0x2 - Minimum valid JPEG segment length (length field size)
  0x100 - Multiplier for big-endian byte[0] (256 = 2^8)
  -0x15 (-21) - Error code for segment too short

functions.name: ParseJpegStartOfFrame
functions.comment:
Parses JPEG Start Of Frame (SOF) marker segment to extract frame header.

Algorithm:
1. Call FUN_6001aa60 to get SOF marker data length from stream
2. Validate data length >= 2 bytes (return 0xFFFFFFEB if too short)
3. Call ReadBytesFromJpegStream to read SOF segment data
4. Extract sample precision from byte 0
5. Extract image height from bytes 1-2 (big-endian)
6. Extract image width from bytes 3-4 (big-endian)
7. Extract number of components from byte 5
8. Free existing component array if present
9. Allocate new component array (16 bytes per component)
10. Parse each component: ID, sampling factors, quant table
11. Track maximum horizontal and vertical sampling factors
12. Calculate MCU dimensions from frame size and max sampling

Parameters:
pbJpegStream - Pointer to JPEG stream/decoder state
pJpegContext - Pointer to JpegImageContext structure

Returns:
0 - Success
0xFFFFFFEB - SOF segment too short
0xFFFFFFF0 - Image height is zero
0xFFFFFFFB - Memory allocation failed

functions.name: ParseJfxxThumbnailData
functions.comment:
Parses JFXX (JFIF Extension) thumbnail data from a JPEG stream.

Algorithm:
1. Call FUN_6001aa60 to initialize stream parsing context
2. Validate stream length (min 14 bytes, max 0x3000E bytes)
3. Call ReadBytesFromJpegStream to extract APP0 segment data
4. Check signature for "JFXX\0" (extension) or "JFIF\0" (standard)
5. Parse thumbnail type byte at offset 5:
   - 0x10: JPEG thumbnail (not processed, skip)
   - 0x11: Palette thumbnail (768-byte RGB palette + indexed pixels)
   - 0x13: RGB24 thumbnail (raw RGB pixels)
6. Extract thumbnail width and height from stream
7. For palette type (0x11):
   - Allocate 768-byte (0x300) palette buffer via operator_new
   - Copy palette data from stream
   - Convert indexed pixels to RGB using palette lookup
8. For RGB24 type (0x13):
   - Copy raw RGB pixel data row-by-row
9. Handle RGB/BGR swap based on pImageCtx->dwComponentType:
   - Type 1: Keep RGB order
   - Other: Swap to BGR order
10. Store thumbnail dimensions in pImageCtx at offset 0x60/0x64
11. Free temporary allocations via AtoiMbcsWrapper (free wrapper)

Parameters:
  pImageCtx - Pointer to JpegImageContext structure containing:
              - offset 0x00: JPEG version (0x14=JFIF 1.4, 0x15=JFIF 1.5)
              - offset 0x20: pDctBaseAddr (output buffer base)
              - offset 0x34: dwComponentType (1=RGB, other=BGR)
              - offset 0x3C: dwBlockStride (row stride in bytes)
              - offset 0x60: dwThumbnailWidth (output)
              - offset 0x64: dwThumbnailHeight (output)
              - offset 0x37DC: thumbnail enable flag
  pbStreamData - Raw JPEG stream data pointer

Returns:
  0 on success
  -21 (0xFFFFFFEB) on stream read error

Magic Numbers Reference:
  0x4A 0x46 0x58 0x58 0x00 = "JFXX\0" signature
  0x4A 0x46 0x49 0x46 0x00 = "JFIF\0" signature
  0x10 = JPEG compressed thumbnail type
  0x11 = Palette-based thumbnail type
  0x13 = RGB24 uncompressed thumbnail type
  0x14/0x15 = JFIF version 1.4/1.5
  0x300 = 768 bytes = 256 colors * 3 bytes (RGB palette size)

functions.name: ParseJpegQuantizationTables
functions.signature: int ParseJpegQuantizationTables(int nDecoderCtx, byte * pStreamCtx, int nSkipDctCompute)
functions.comment:
Parses JPEG DQT (Define Quantization Table) marker segment and populates quantization tables.

Algorithm:
1. Read segment length from stream using FUN_6001aa60.
2. Validate segment length is between 2 and 517 bytes (0x205).
3. Read quantization table data from JPEG stream via ReadBytesFromJpegStream.
4. For each table entry in segment:
   a. Extract table index (low nibble, 0-4) and precision (high nibble).
   b. Validate table index is in range 0-4.
   c. Store precision at component offset +0x94.
   d. Update component count at decoder offset +0x84 if needed.
   e. Copy quantization values to table at component offset +0x9c.
   f. If not skipping DCT, call ComputeDctCoefficientsZigzag.
5. Free allocated buffer if any.

Parameters:
  nDecoderCtx - Pointer to JPEG decoder context structure (cast as int).
  pStreamCtx - Pointer to JPEG stream context for reading.
  nSkipDctCompute - If non-zero, skip DCT coefficient zigzag computation.

Returns:
  0 on success.
  -21 (0xFFFFFFEB) if segment length out of valid range.
  -7 (0xFFFFFFF9) if table index greater than 4 (invalid quantization table ID).
  Other negative values from ReadBytesFromJpegStream or FUN_6001aa60.

Structure Layout (Decoder Context):
  Offset  Size  Field         Description
  0x80    4     dwTableCount  Number of quantization tables processed.
  0x84    4     dwCompCount   Number of components with quantization tables.

Structure Layout (Component, stride 0xB4):
  Offset  Size  Field         Description
  0x94    4     dwPrecision   Quantization precision (0=8-bit, 1=16-bit).
  0x9c    4     pQuantTable   Pointer to 64-entry quantization table.

Magic Numbers:
  0x205 (517) - Maximum DQT segment length.
  0x40 (64) - Quantization table entry count.
  0x41 (65) - 8-bit table size (1 header + 64 bytes).
  0x81 (129) - 16-bit table size (1 header + 128 bytes).
  0xB4 (180) - Component structure stride.

functions.name: ParseDhtMarkerSegment
functions.comment:
Parses a JPEG DHT (Define Huffman Table) marker segment and builds Huffman decode tables.

Algorithm:
1. Validate marker data pointer and read segment length from stream
2. Subtract 2-byte length field, verify remaining data is within valid DHT size (0x2-0x445)
3. Read DHT segment bytes from JPEG stream into allocated buffer
4. For each Huffman table definition in segment:
   a. Extract table class (AC=1/DC=0) from upper nibble of first byte
   b. Extract table destination ID (0-3) from lower nibble
   c. Validate class is 0 or 1, destination is 0-3
   d. Track max destination IDs used at context offsets 0x88 (DC) and 0x8c (AC)
   e. Call BuildHuffmanDecodeTable with code lengths and symbol values
   f. Sum 16 code length bytes to get symbol count
   g. Advance past this table definition (17 header bytes + symbol count)
5. Free allocated buffer if allocation flag set

Parameters:
  pJpegDecoder - Pointer to JPEG decoder context structure containing Huffman tables
  pbMarkerData - Pointer to DHT marker data (after 0xFFC4 marker bytes)

Returns:
  0 on success
  -6 (0xFFFFFFFA) if table class or destination ID out of range
  -21 (0xFFFFFFEB) if segment length invalid (too small or too large)
  Other negative values from called functions on error

Structure Layout (pJpegDecoder offsets):
  Offset   Size   Field               Description
  0x088    4      dwDcTableCount      Number of DC Huffman tables defined
  0x08C    4      dwAcTableCount      Number of AC Huffman tables defined
  0x090    4      dwMaxTableId        Maximum table destination ID + 1
  0x364    0x670  aDcTables[4]        DC Huffman decode tables (4 x HuffmanDecodeTable)
  0x1D24   0x670  aAcTables[4]        AC Huffman decode tables (4 x HuffmanDecodeTable)

Magic Numbers:
  0x2 - Minimum DHT segment length (length field only)
  0x444 - Maximum DHT segment data after length (1092 bytes)
  0x11 (17) - DHT table header size (1 class/id byte + 16 code length bytes)
  0x670 (1648) - Size of each HuffmanDecodeTable structure
  0x364, 0x1D24 - Context offsets to DC and AC table arrays

Decompiler Notes:
  SSA temporaries (iVar2, iVar3, iVar5, bVar1, pbVar4) are register-allocated
  intermediate values that cannot be renamed:
  - iVar2: Return value / error code accumulator
  - iVar3: Sum of code length bytes (symbol count)
  - iVar5: Loop counter for 16 code length bytes
  - bVar1: Table class byte (upper nibble of table header)
  - pbVar4: Temporary pointer for stream operations

functions.name: ParseJpegFrameHeader
functions.signature: int ParseJpegFrameHeader(byte * pDecoderContext, byte * pbStreamData, byte * pFrameInfo, uint * pComponentInfo)
functions.comment:
Parses JPEG SOF (Start Of Frame) marker to extract frame header information.
Reads component count, allocates component table, and populates component entries
with sampling factors, quantization table pointers, and Huffman table pointers.

Algorithm:
1. Read 2-byte segment length (big-endian) via ReadBigEndian16FromJpegStream
2. Validate segment length >= 2 bytes, return -21 (0xFFFFFFEB) if invalid
3. Read frame header data from stream via ReadBytesFromJpegStream
4. Extract component count from first byte, store in pComponentInfo[0]
5. Allocate component table: count * 24 bytes via operator_new
6. Store table pointer at pComponentInfo[0xD] (offset 0x34)
7. Loop through each component:
   a. Read component ID byte
   b. Read sampling factors byte (H=high nibble, V=low nibble)
   c. Validate H and V sampling factors are in range 0-4
   d. Search pFrameInfo component array for matching component ID
   e. Populate component entry (24 bytes each):
      - [0x00]: Table index
      - [0x04]: Sampling factor H
      - [0x08]: Sampling factor V
      - [0x0C]: Quantization table ptr (pDecoderContext + 0x1D24 + idx*0x670)
      - [0x10]: DC Huffman table ptr (pDecoderContext + 0x364 + idx*0x670)
      - [0x14]: AC Huffman table ptr (pDecoderContext + 0x94 + idx*0xB4)
8. Read sample precision, image height, chroma sampling into pComponentInfo
9. Free temporary buffer if allocated

Parameters:
pDecoderContext - JPEG decoder context base address containing Huffman/quant tables
pbStreamData    - Stream context pointer for reading JPEG data
pFrameInfo      - Frame info structure with component tables at offset +0x28
pComponentInfo  - OUT: Receives parsed frame data and allocated component table

Returns:
0              - Success
-5 (0xFFFFFFFB) - Memory allocation failure
-21 (0xFFFFFFEB) - Invalid segment length or sampling factor out of range

Structure Layout (pComponentInfo output):
Offset  Size  Field              Description
0x00    4     dwComponentCount   Number of color components
0x08    4     dwSamplePrecision  Bits per sample
0x0C    4     dwImageHeight      Image height in pixels
0x10    4     dwHChroma          Horizontal chroma sampling
0x14    4     dwVChroma          Vertical chroma sampling
0x34    4     pComponentTable    Pointer to allocated component array

Component Entry Layout (24 bytes each):
Offset  Size  Field           Description
0x00    4     nTableIndex     Index into frame component array
0x04    4     nSamplingH      Horizontal sampling factor
0x08    4     nSamplingV      Vertical sampling factor
0x0C    4     pQuantTable     Pointer to quantization table
0x10    4     pDcHuffman      Pointer to DC Huffman table
0x14    4     pAcHuffman      Pointer to AC Huffman table

Magic Numbers:
0x1D24 - Quantization table base offset in decoder context
0x364  - DC Huffman table base offset in decoder context
0x94   - AC Huffman table base offset in decoder context
0x670  - Stride between consecutive table entries
0xB4   - AC Huffman table stride
0x18   - Size of component entry structure (24 bytes)

Note: dwSehEspBackup is an SEH stack frame variable (stores ESP backup).
Type cannot be set via decompiler due to Ghidra HighVariable limitation.

functions.name: WriteJfifApp0Marker
functions.comment:
Writes the JFIF APP0 marker segment to the JPEG output stream.

Algorithm:
1. Initialize 20-byte marker data buffer on stack
2. Write APP0 marker prefix (0xE0) to output via FUN_6001b8b0
3. Write APP0 length field (0x10 = 16 bytes) via FUN_6001b8d0
4. Build JFIF signature: 'J' (0x4A), 'F' (0x46), 'I' (0x49), 'F' (0x46), null
5. Write JFIF version 1.1: Major=1, Minor=1
6. Write density units byte: 0 (aspect ratio only, no physical units)
7. Write thumbnail dimensions: X=0, Y=0 (no embedded thumbnail)
8. Flush buffered marker data via FUN_6001b8d0
9. Call g_pfnDecodeProc1 to output complete 18-byte APP0 segment

Parameters:
  pOutputBuffer (byte*) - Destination buffer for encoded JPEG stream data

Returns:
  void - No return value; output written directly to buffer via callback

Magic Numbers:
  0xE0 - JPEG APP0 marker identifier
  0x10 - APP0 segment payload length (16 bytes, excludes marker)
  0x12 - Total APP0 segment size (18 bytes including length field)
  0x4A,0x46,0x49,0x46,0x00 - "JFIF" null-terminated identifier
  0x01,0x01 - JFIF version 1.1 (major, minor)

JFIF APP0 Marker Layout:
  Offset  Size  Field           Value
  0       2     Marker          0xFFE0 (written by caller)
  2       2     Length          0x0010 (16 bytes)
  4       5     Identifier      "JFIF\0"
  9       1     Version Major   0x01
  10      1     Version Minor   0x01
  11      1     DensityUnits    0x00 (aspect ratio)
  12      2     Xdensity        (set elsewhere)
  14      2     Ydensity        (set elsewhere)
  16      1     Xthumbnail      0x00
  17      1     Ythumbnail      0x00

functions.name: WriteMarkerByte
functions.comment:
Writes a JPEG marker byte sequence to the output buffer.

Algorithm:
1. Write the marker prefix byte (0xFF) at current buffer position
2. Increment buffer position
3. Write the marker type byte at the new position
4. Increment buffer position again

Parameters:
  param_1 (bMarkerType) - BYTE: The JPEG marker type identifier (e.g., 0xD8 for SOI, 0xE0 for APP0)
  param_2 (pnBufferPos) - int*: Pointer to the current write position in the output buffer

Returns:
  void - Buffer position is updated via the pnBufferPos pointer

Magic Numbers:
  0xFF - Standard JPEG marker prefix byte

Notes:
  JPEG markers always consist of 0xFF followed by a marker type byte.
  Called by various JPEG segment writing functions (SOI, APP0, SOF0, SOS, etc.).

functions.name: WriteMarkerWord
functions.comment:
Writes a 16-bit marker word to a JPEG output buffer in big-endian format.

Algorithm:
1. Extract high byte (bits 8-15) from marker word using right shift
2. Write high byte to current buffer position
3. Increment buffer position pointer
4. Write low byte (bits 0-7) to next buffer position  
5. Increment buffer position pointer again

Parameters:
  dwMarkerWord - 16-bit JPEG marker value (e.g., 0xFFD8 for SOI, 0xFFE0 for APP0)
  pnBufferPos  - Pointer to current write position in output buffer (updated on return)

Returns:
  void - Buffer position pointer is incremented by 2 bytes on return

Special Cases:
  - Caller must ensure buffer has at least 2 bytes available
  - Buffer position pointer must be valid and writable

Magic Numbers Reference:
  - 0x8: Bit shift for extracting high byte from 16-bit value

Called By:
  WriteJfifApp0Marker, WriteSof0Marker, WriteQuantizationTableMarker,
  WriteHuffmanTableMarkers, WriteSosMarker, WriteRestartIntervalMarker

functions.name: WriteSoiMarkerAndInitEncoder
functions.comment:
Writes the JPEG SOI (Start of Image) marker and initializes the encoder state.

Algorithm:
1. Allocate a 4-byte local buffer (abMarkerBytes) for marker construction
2. Set buffer pointer (pbMarkerBuffer) to point to local buffer
3. Call WriteMarkerByte to write SOI marker (0xFFD8) to output stream
4. Call g_pfnDecodeProc1 function pointer to initialize encoder with buffer and state

Parameters:
  pEncoderState - Pointer to JPEG encoder state structure (offset from main JPEG state)

Returns:
  void - No return value

Local Variables:
  abMarkerBytes (byte[4]) - Stack buffer at [ESP] for marker byte construction
  pbMarkerBuffer (byte *) - Pointer at [ESP+4] initialized to abMarkerBytes address

Magic Numbers:
  0xD8 - JPEG SOI (Start of Image) marker byte (preceded by 0xFF)
  0x02 - Encoder initialization mode passed to g_pfnDecodeProc1

Called By:
  ProcessJpegEncodeScan - Called for non-progressive encoding modes (not types 8 or 9)

Related Functions:
  WriteMarkerByte - Writes 0xFF prefix byte followed by marker byte
  g_pfnDecodeProc1 - Function pointer for encoder state initialization

functions.name: WriteEoiMarkerAndFlushEncoder
functions.comment:
Writes the JPEG EOI (End of Image) marker and flushes the encoder output buffer.

Algorithm:
1. Allocate 4-byte local buffer for marker construction
2. Set buffer pointer to point to local buffer start
3. Call WriteMarkerByte to write EOI marker (0xFF 0xD9) to buffer
4. Call g_pfnDecodeProc1 to flush 2 bytes from buffer to encoder output stream

Parameters:
  pEncoderState (int *) - Pointer to JPEG encoder state structure (offset 0xDFA from main state)

Returns:
  void - No return value

Local Variables:
  abMarkerBytes (byte[4]) - Stack buffer at [ESP] for marker byte construction
  pbMarkerBuffer (byte *) - Pointer at [ESP+0x4] tracking current write position in buffer

Magic Numbers:
  0xD9 - JPEG EOI (End of Image) marker byte (preceded by 0xFF written by WriteMarkerByte)
  0x02 - Number of bytes to flush (the 2-byte EOI marker: 0xFF 0xD9)

Related Functions:
  WriteMarkerByte - Writes 0xFF prefix followed by marker byte to buffer
  WriteSoiMarkerAndInitEncoder - Writes SOI marker (0xD8) at stream start
  g_pfnDecodeProc1 - Function pointer for flushing buffer to output stream

Called By:
  ProcessJpegEncodeScan - Called when all scans complete (nScanResult == 0)
  FUN_60017980 - Called for non-progressive encoding modes

functions.name: WriteSof0Marker
functions.comment:
Writes JPEG SOF0 (Start Of Frame - Baseline DCT) marker segment to output stream.

Algorithm:
1. Calculate segment length as (component_count * 3) + 8
2. Write 0xFF 0xC0 marker bytes via WriteMarkerByte
3. Write segment length as big-endian word via WriteMarkerWord
4. Write sample precision (8 bits per sample)
5. Write image height and width as big-endian words
6. Write component count
7. For each component, write component ID, sampling factors, and quantization table selector
8. Output complete buffer via g_pfnDecodeProc1 function pointer

Parameters:
pOutputStream - JpegOutputBuffer*: Output stream buffer for encoded data
pJpegContext - JpegImageContext*: JPEG encoding context structure
  +0x04: Image height (uint)
  +0x08: Image width (uint)
  +0x1C: Component count (1=grayscale, 3=color)
  +0x28: Pointer to component info array (16 bytes per component)

Returns:
void - No return value

Magic Numbers:
0xC0 - SOF0 marker (Start Of Frame, Baseline DCT)
0x08 - Sample precision (8 bits per component)
0x11 - Sampling factors 1x1 horizontal and vertical
0x10 - Component info structure stride (16 bytes per entry)

functions.name: WriteQuantizationTableMarker
functions.signature: void WriteQuantizationTableMarker(undefined4 pJpegContext, char cPrecision, char cTableId, byte * pbQuantizationTable)
functions.comment:
Writes a JPEG DQT (Define Quantization Table) marker segment to the output stream.

Algorithm:
1. Initialize local buffer pointer to stack-allocated marker data buffer
2. Write DQT marker byte (0xDB) to buffer via WriteMarkerByte
3. Write segment length (0x43 = 67 bytes) via WriteMarkerWord
4. Combine precision (upper 4 bits) and table ID (lower 4 bits) into single byte
5. Copy 64 quantization values from source table with stride 2 (zigzag reordering)
6. Call encoder output function to write completed segment to output

Parameters:
pJpegContext - JpegImageContext pointer passed to output callback function
cPrecision - Quantization value precision (0=8-bit, 1=16-bit), stored in upper nibble
cTableId - Quantization table destination ID (0-3), stored in lower nibble
pbQuantizationTable - Source quantization table with values at stride 2 (interleaved zigzag order)

Returns:
void - No return value, marker data written through callback

Special Cases:
Source table uses stride 2 to skip zigzag index bytes in interleaved format
Buffer size 72 bytes accommodates marker plus length plus precision/id plus 64 values

Magic Numbers:
0xDB - JPEG DQT (Define Quantization Table) marker
0x43 - Segment length 67 bytes (2 length + 1 precision/id + 64 values)
0x10 - Shift value for 4-bit precision field (cPrecision * 16)
0x40 - Loop count for 64 quantization table entries
0x45 - Output callback command flag for write operation

functions.name: WriteHuffmanTableMarkers
functions.comment:
Writes DHT (Define Huffman Table) markers to JPEG output stream.

Algorithm:
1. Calculate total symbol count by summing bit lengths across all tables
2. Write DHT marker header (0xFFC4) with calculated segment length
3. Call output proc to write initial 4-byte marker header
4. For each Huffman table (DC and AC pairs):
   a. Sum bit length counts (16 bytes) to get symbol count
   b. Validate total size does not exceed 0x144 bytes
   c. Build table header: (table_class << 4) | table_id
   d. Copy 16 bit-length bytes to buffer
   e. Copy symbol values to buffer
   f. Call output proc to write table data

Parameters:
    pOutputBuffer - Pointer to JPEG output buffer/stream context
    pJpegEncoder - Pointer to JPEG encoder context containing Huffman tables

Returns:
    0 - Success
    -6 (0xFFFFFFFA) - Table size exceeds maximum (0x144 bytes)
    Other - Error code from output procedure

Magic Numbers:
    0xC4 - DHT marker type (second byte after 0xFF)
    0x10 - Number of bit-length counts per table (16 bits max code length)
    0x11 - Header size: 16 bit-lengths + 1 table identifier byte
    0x22 - Per-table overhead: 0x11 * 2 bytes
    0x90 - Offset to Huffman table count in encoder context
    0x373C - Offset to Huffman table entry array in encoder context
    0x144 - Maximum allowed table segment size (324 bytes)
    0x0C - Huffman table entry stride (12 bytes per entry)

functions.name: WriteSosMarker
functions.signature: void WriteSosMarker(int * pEncoderState, int nComponents, byte * pbDcTableSelectors, byte * pbAcTableSelectors)
functions.comment:
Writes the JPEG SOS (Start of Scan) marker segment to the encoder buffer.

Algorithm:
1. Calculate marker data length as nComponents * 2 + 6 bytes
2. Write 0xDA (SOS marker identifier) via WriteMarkerByte
3. Write marker length word via WriteMarkerWord
4. Write number of scan components (Ns)
5. For grayscale (1 component):
   a. Write component ID 0
   b. Write combined Huffman selector 0x00 (DC=0, AC=0)
6. For YCbCr (3+ components):
   a. Write component ID 1 with first DC/AC selector pair
   b. For components 2 to nComponents, write ID and combined selectors
   c. Combined selector = (DC_table << 4) | AC_table
7. Write spectral selection: Ss=0, Se=0x3F (63), Ah/Al=0
8. Call g_pfnDecodeProc1 to process complete marker buffer

Parameters:
  pEncoderState - Pointer to encoder state structure (passed to g_pfnDecodeProc1)
  nComponents - Number of color components (1=grayscale, 3=YCbCr)
  pbDcTableSelectors - Array of DC Huffman table indices per component
  pbAcTableSelectors - Array of AC Huffman table indices per component

Returns:
  void - No return value

Magic Numbers:
  0xDA - JPEG SOS (Start of Scan) marker identifier
  0x3F (63) - End spectral selection (Se) for baseline DCT
  6 - Base marker length (2 length + 1 Ns + 3 spectral bytes)
  0x10 (16) - DC table index left shift amount for combining

functions.name: WriteRestartIntervalMarker
functions.comment:
Writes the JPEG DRI (Define Restart Interval) marker to the output stream.

Algorithm:
1. Allocate 6-byte buffer on stack for marker data
2. Write marker header: 0xFF followed by 0xDD (DRI marker identifier)
3. Write marker length: 0x0004 (4 bytes, big-endian)
4. Write restart interval value as 2-byte big-endian integer
5. Call g_pfnDecodeProc1 to flush 6-byte buffer to output stream

Parameters:
- nRestartInterval: Number of MCUs between restart markers (0 disables restart markers)
- pScanState: Pointer to scan state structure containing output buffer context

Returns:
- Return value from g_pfnDecodeProc1 (0 on success, non-zero on error)

JPEG Marker Structure (6 bytes total):
Offset  Size  Field              Value
0x00    1     Marker prefix      0xFF
0x01    1     Marker type        0xDD (DRI)
0x02    2     Length             0x0004 (big-endian)
0x04    2     Restart interval   nRestartInterval (big-endian)

Special Cases:
- Restart interval of 0 means no restart markers in the JPEG stream
- Called during progressive JPEG encoding setup (from FUN_600179f0)

functions.name: WriteRestartMarkerAndDecode
functions.comment:
Writes a JPEG restart marker and invokes the decode procedure.

Converts a restart marker index (0-7) to the corresponding JPEG RST marker byte
(0xD0-0xD7) and writes it to the output stream, then continues decoding.

Algorithm:
1. Validate restart index is in range 0-7 (RST0-RST7)
2. Convert index to marker byte (0xD0 + index) via switch statement
3. Setup write position pointer to parameter stack location
4. Write marker sequence via FUN_6001b8b0 (writes 0xFF + marker byte)
5. Call g_pfnDecodeProc1 to continue decoding from new position
6. Return decode result or error code for invalid index

Parameters:
nRestartIndex (dword): Restart marker index (0-7)
  - 0 = RST0 (0xD0), 1 = RST1 (0xD1), ... 7 = RST7 (0xD7)
  - Values > 7 return error immediately
pScanState (void*): Pointer to scan state structure for decoding context

Returns:
0: Success - decode completed normally
Non-zero positive: Decode procedure return value (suspension or continuation)
-25 (0xFFFFFFE7): Invalid restart marker index (out of range 0-7)

Magic Numbers:
0xD0-0xD7: JPEG RST0-RST7 restart marker bytes
0xFFFFFFE7: -25 decimal, invalid restart index error
0x02: Decode mode parameter passed to g_pfnDecodeProc1

Special Cases:
- Index > 7 returns immediately with error, no marker written
- Compiler optimized switch statement for index-to-marker conversion

functions.name: DecodeJpegScanDispatch
functions.signature: int DecodeJpegScanDispatch(int * pnBytesDecoded, uint * pFrameInfo, int * pBitStream, int * pScanState)
functions.comment:
Dispatches JPEG scan decoding to appropriate handler based on DCT mode and bit depth.

Algorithm:
1. Initialize output bytes decoded to zero
2. Check if scan progress is within bounds (scan lines, spectral selection)
3. If within bounds, dispatch to immediate scan decode (baseline or progressive DCT)
4. If out of bounds, clamp scan parameters to valid range
5. Allocate MCU working buffer (0x50000 bytes) if not already allocated
6. Initialize MCU buffer header with frame dimensions and reset all entries
7. Dispatch to MCU block decoder (baseline or progressive)
8. Call decode completion callback on success
9. Return result code

Parameters:
    pnBytesDecoded (int*) - OUT: Number of bytes successfully decoded
    pFrameInfo (uint*) - IN: JPEG frame information structure
    pBitStream (int*) - IN: Bit stream reader state
    pScanState (int*) - IN/OUT: Scan decoder state structure

Returns:
    0 on success
    -5 on memory allocation failure
    Other negative values on decode error

Magic Numbers:
    0x50000 - MCU working buffer size (327680 bytes, ~8192 MCU entries)
    0x28 - MCU entry stride (40 bytes per entry)
    0x120C - Offset to MCU buffer pointer in scan state (index 4620)
    0x1378 - Offset to progressive mode flag in scan state (index 4984)

JPEG Mode Dispatch (scan state[0]):
    0x0E, 0x0F: 2-bit depth
    0x10, 0x11: 4-bit depth
    0x12, 0x13: 8-bit depth
    default: 1-bit depth

functions.name: ProcessProgressiveDctScanBlocks
functions.signature: int ProcessProgressiveDctScanBlocks(uint * pnOutputBuffer, uint * pScanBuffer, int * pComponentInfo, int nDecoderContext, uint dwPrecisionMode)
functions.comment:
Processes DCT (Discrete Cosine Transform) blocks for JPEG progressive scan decoding.

Algorithm:
1. Initialize component information arrays (block widths, quant table pointers, block counts)
2. Calculate total block count from component structure at offset 0x37c0
3. Branch based on component mode (interleaved vs non-interleaved)
4. For each MCU row and column:
   a. Calculate coefficient buffer offset using (row * width + col) * blockCount * 128
   b. Clear or decode DCT coefficients based on component settings
   c. Apply inverse DCT transform based on precision mode switch
   d. Call FUN_6001cc30 to process decoded blocks
   e. Update row/column state for progressive decoding
5. Handle scan boundary conditions and resumption state for streaming

Parameters:
- pnOutputBuffer: Output buffer for decoded image data (unused in some paths)
- pScanBuffer: Input scan buffer with encoded DCT coefficients  
- pComponentInfo: JPEG component descriptor structure
  - [0]: Number of components in scan
  - [2],[3]: Component dimensions (0 indicates non-interleaved mode)
  - [4]: Interleave flag (0=non-interleaved, non-zero=interleaved)
  - [5]: Successive approximation bit position
  - [7]: Current column position in MCU grid
  - [8]: Current row position in MCU grid
  - [0xd]: Pointer to component info sub-structure array
- nDecoderContext: JPEG decoder context structure base address
  - +0x4,+0x8,+0xc,+0x10: Resume state column/row positions
  - +0x1c: Streaming interrupt flag (non-zero triggers save/resume)
  - +0x4c: Maximum horizontal block coordinate
  - +0x50: Maximum vertical block coordinate
  - +0x78: Horizontal MCU count per row
  - +0x7c: Vertical MCU count (total rows)
  - +0x37c0: Number of components in current scan
  - +0x37cc: Pointer to scan component info array
  - +0x37d4,+0x37d8: Scan spectral start/end positions
  - +0x4834: Coefficient dequantization working buffer pointer
  - +0x4de4: DCT coefficient storage buffer pointer
- dwPrecisionMode: DCT precision and transform mode selector
  - 1: Full 8x8 IDCT via PerformInverseDiscreteCosineTransform8x8
  - 2: 4x4 scaled IDCT via FUN_600129e0
  - 4: 2x2 scaled IDCT via FUN_60012c50
  - 8: DC-only mode with direct scaling and rounding

Returns:
- 0: Success - scan processing complete
- 1: Partial decode - streaming interrupted, resume state saved
- -25 (0xFFFFFFE7): Decode error from FUN_6001cc30

Magic Numbers:
- 0x80 (128): Size of one 8x8 DCT block in bytes (64 coefficients * 2 bytes)
- 0x40 (64): Number of coefficients per 8x8 DCT block
- 8: Rounding bias for DC-only scaling ((val + 8) >> 4)
- 4: Right shift count for DC scaling (divide by 16)

Special Cases:
- Non-interleaved mode (component[2]==0 or [3]==0): Process each component independently
- Interleaved mode: Process all components together in MCU order
- Streaming mode (context+0x1c != 0): Can pause mid-decode and resume later

functions.name: CheckRestartIntervalBoundary
functions.signature: int CheckRestartIntervalBoundary(byte * pBitstreamState, uint * pScanInfo, int nJpegContext, int nBlockColumn, int nBlockRow)
functions.comment:
Checks if the current block position falls on a restart interval boundary and processes the restart marker if needed.

Algorithm:
1. Check if restart interval is enabled (pScanInfo[0x18] != 0)
2. Calculate absolute block position: (blocks_per_row * nBlockRow) + nBlockColumn + 1
3. Check if position is divisible by restart interval (modulo check)
4. Verify position is within total block count bounds
5. Reset all 4 DC prediction coefficients in scan info (offsets 0x24-0x30)
6. Clear the accumulated bits counter in bitstream state (offset 0xc)
7. If marker already pending (bMarkerPending != 0), clear flag and return success
8. Otherwise call ReadNextJpegMarkerCode to read and validate the restart marker

Parameters:
  pBitstreamState - Bitstream reader state containing bit buffer and marker flags
  pScanInfo       - Current scan processing state with restart interval and DC predictions
  nJpegContext    - JPEG decoder context with image dimensions and component info
  nBlockColumn    - Current MCU block column index (X position)
  nBlockRow       - Current MCU block row index (Y position)

Returns:
  0               - No restart boundary, or restart processed successfully
  Non-zero        - Error code from ReadNextJpegMarkerCode (marker validation failed)

Structure Layout:
  pScanInfo:
    +0x18  dwRestartInterval  uint    Restart interval in MCU blocks (0=disabled)
    +0x24  nDcPred0           int     DC prediction for component 0
    +0x28  nDcPred1           int     DC prediction for component 1  
    +0x2c  nDcPred2           int     DC prediction for component 2
    +0x30  nDcPred3           int     DC prediction for component 3

  pBitstreamState:
    +0x0c  dwAccumulatedBits  uint    Accumulated bits counter (cleared on restart)
    +0x30  bMarkerPending     byte    Flag indicating marker already detected

  nJpegContext:
    +0x78  nBlocksPerRow      int     Number of MCU blocks per row
    +0x7c  nTotalBlockRows    int     Total number of MCU block rows

functions.name: ProcessMcuBlocksDecode
functions.signature: int ProcessMcuBlocksDecode(uint * pBitstream, uint * pHuffmanState, int * pScanInfo, int nJpegContext, int nIdctScale)
functions.comment:
Processes JPEG MCU (Minimum Coded Unit) blocks during decoding with configurable IDCT scaling.

Algorithm:
1. Initialize component data arrays from scan info structure (blocks per component, quantization tables, DCT buffers)
2. Compute MCU grid boundaries based on image dimensions and IDCT scale factor (8/nIdctScale)
3. Calculate total DCT blocks from component sampling factors
4. Branch based on progressive vs sequential scan mode (pScanInfo[2] and pScanInfo[3])
5. For sequential mode: iterate over MCU rows and columns
   a. For first spectral selection (DC): call memset to init block, decode with FUN_60014150
   b. For subsequent AC bands: decode with FUN_60014220
   c. Copy coefficients to temp buffer, perform scaled IDCT based on nIdctScale
   d. Call FUN_6001cc30 for restart marker processing
   e. Call output routines (FUN_600021b0 or FUN_600038b0) for color conversion
6. For progressive mode: similar flow with hierarchical coefficient accumulation
7. Update scan progress state for interleaved/restart processing

Parameters:
  pBitstream    - Bitstream reader state for entropy coded data
  pHuffmanState - Huffman decoding state and coefficient storage
  pScanInfo     - Scan header info (component count, spectral selection, successive approximation)
  nJpegContext  - JPEG decoder context containing image dimensions and component info
  nIdctScale    - IDCT output scale factor (1=8x8, 2=4x4, 4=2x2, 8=1x1)

Returns:
  -25 (0xFFFFFFE7) - Error during restart marker processing (FUN_6001cc30 failed)
  0                - Scan completed, reached end of image
  1                - Partial decode, more MCUs remaining (for restart processing)
  2                - Scan completed successfully with full coefficient accumulation

Special Cases:
  - Single component images force blocks-per-component to 1
  - Progressive scans check coefficient accumulation thresholds before IDCT
  - Restart marker handling updates x/y position and returns early

Magic Numbers Reference:
  0x80   - DCT block size in bytes (64 coefficients * 2 bytes each)
  0x40   - 64 coefficients per 8x8 DCT block
  0x18   - Component descriptor stride (24 bytes per component)
  0x37b8 - Offset to max H sampling factor in context
  0x37bc - Offset to max V sampling factor in context
  0x37c0 - Offset to number of components in context
  0x37cc - Offset to component info array in context
  0x37d4 - Offset to DC coefficient count in context
  0x37d8 - Offset to AC coefficient count in context
  0x37e0 - Offset to EOB run flag in context
  0x4834 - Offset to temporary DCT buffer pointer in context
  0x4de4 - Offset to coefficient storage base pointer in context

functions.name: ProcessBaselineDctScanBlocks
functions.signature: int ProcessBaselineDctScanBlocks(int * pnResult, byte * pBitstream, int * pScanInfo, int nDecoderContext, int nOutputPrecision)
functions.comment:
Decodes baseline DCT scan blocks for JPEG image decompression.

Processes Minimum Coded Units (MCUs) by decoding entropy-coded DCT coefficients,
applying inverse discrete cosine transforms (IDCT), and writing output pixels.

Algorithm:
1. Initialize component block counts from scan information header
2. Calculate MCU grid dimensions based on component count and image size
3. For single component, compute MCU dimensions from sample factors
4. Loop through MCU rows (Y) and columns (X)
5. For each MCU, decode all DCT blocks for each component via g_pfnDecodeProc19
6. Check restart marker synchronization via FUN_6001cc30
7. Apply IDCT transform based on output precision mode:
   - Mode 1: Full 8x8 IDCT via g_pfnIdct8x8, then output via FUN_600021b0
   - Mode 2: 4-bit output IDCT via FUN_600129e0
   - Mode 4: 2-bit output IDCT via FUN_60012c50
   - Mode 8: 1-bit output with DC-only scaling
8. Write output samples via FUN_600038b0 for modes 2/4/8
9. Handle restart interval state update

Parameters:
  pnResult - Output result pointer (unused in baseline mode)
  pBitstream - Pointer to bitstream context for entropy decoding
  pScanInfo - Scan information structure containing:
    [0x00] Component count
    [0x1C] Current MCU X position
    [0x20] Current MCU Y position
    [0x24] DC predictor values array
    [0x34] Component info table pointer
  nDecoderContext - Decoder context structure containing:
    [0x1C] Restart interval enable flag
    [0x4C] Image width in pixels
    [0x50] Image height in pixels (signed)
    [0x78] MCU columns count
    [0x7C] MCU rows count
    [0x37B8] Max horizontal samples
    [0x37BC] Max vertical samples
    [0x4834] DCT coefficient buffer pointer
  nOutputPrecision - Output bit depth mode (1=8-bit, 2=4-bit, 4=2-bit, 8=1-bit)

Returns:
  0 - Success, all MCUs decoded
  1 - Partial decode, restart interval triggered
  -21 (0xFFFFFFEB) - Decode error from entropy decoder
  -25 (0xFFFFFFE7) - Restart marker synchronization error

Magic Numbers:
  0x80 - DCT block coefficient buffer stride (64 shorts * 2 bytes)
  0x40 - DCT block pointer increment (64 coefficient entries)
  8 - DCT block dimensions (8x8)

functions.name: DecodeJpegScanData
functions.signature: int DecodeJpegScanData(undefined4 pJpegProps, byte * pBitStream, int * pScanInfo, int * pFrameInfo, int nScaleFactor)
functions.comment:
Decodes JPEG scan data performing MCU-based entropy decoding and IDCT transformation.

This is the core JPEG scan decoder that processes compressed scan data from a
bitstream, decodes Huffman-coded coefficients for each component, performs
inverse discrete cosine transform (IDCT), and writes output to destination buffers.
Supports multiple scale factors (1:1, 1:2, 1:4, 1:8) for progressive decoding.

Algorithm:
1. Initialize component block counts and DC coefficient pointers from scan info
2. Calculate scaled MCU dimensions based on sampling factors and scale factor
3. Determine horizontal/vertical block counts for output grid
4. For single-component scans: calculate direct output dimensions
5. For multi-component scans: use pre-calculated MCU grid from frame info
6. Loop through MCU rows (Y) and columns (X):
   a. For each component in scan, decode all blocks using g_pfnDecodeProc
   b. Call ProcessMcuBlock to process decoded MCU data
   c. Check restart interval boundaries if applicable
7. For full MCU rows, perform IDCT based on scale factor:
   - Scale 1: Full 8x8 IDCT via g_pfnIdct8x8
   - Scale 2: 4x4 IDCT
   - Scale 4: 2x2 IDCT  
   - Scale 8: 1x1 DC-only scaling
8. Copy transformed blocks to output buffer via CopyBlocksToOutput_*
9. Update partial decode state for incremental decoding support

Parameters:
  pJpegProps    - JPEG_CORE_PROPERTIES* context with decoder state, sampling factors,
                  output buffers, and restart interval configuration at offset 0x37e0
  pBitStream    - byte* pointer to compressed bitstream data
  pScanInfo     - int* scan header info: [0]=component count, [0x1c]=partial row,
                  [0x20]=partial col, [0x24+]=DC coefficient pointers per component,
                  [0x34]=component descriptor array
  pFrameInfo    - int* frame header with MCU grid dimensions at [0x78], [0x7c]
  nScaleFactor  - int downscale factor: 1=full size, 2=1/2, 4=1/4, 8=1/8

Returns:
  0  - Success, scan fully decoded
  1  - Partial decode completed (incremental decoding in progress)
  2  - Scan complete, more data available
  -21 (0xFFFFFFEB) - Decode error from Huffman/entropy decoder
  -25 (0xFFFFFFE7) - MCU processing error

Stack Layout (local arrays):
  Offset  Size  Name              Description
  -0x10   16    anHSampFactors    Horizontal sampling factors per component (int[4])
  -0x20   16    anVSampFactors    Vertical sampling factors per component (int[4])
  -0x30   16    adBlockCounts     Block counts per component for iteration (uint[4])

Magic Numbers:
  0x37b8 - Horizontal sampling factor max in JPEG_CORE_PROPERTIES
  0x37bc - Vertical sampling factor max in JPEG_CORE_PROPERTIES  
  0x37e0 - Restart interval enabled flag
  0x4830 - Restart marker table pointer
  0x4834 - DCT coefficient buffer pointer
  0x80   - DCT block size in bytes (64 coefficients * 2 bytes)
  0x28   - Restart table entry stride (40 bytes)

Called By: DecodeJpegScanDispatch
Calls: g_pfnDecodeProc (entropy decoder), g_pfnIdct8x8/4x4 (IDCT),
       ProcessMcuBlock, CopyBlocksToOutput_8x8/4x4/2x2/1x1,
       InitializeMcuRowFromRestartTable

functions.name: InitializeMcuRowFromRestartTable
functions.signature: int InitializeMcuRowFromRestartTable(int nMcuRowIndex, dword * pBitStream, int * pScanInfo, int * pFrameInfo)
functions.comment:
Initializes MCU (Minimum Coded Unit) row parameters from the restart marker table.

Copies scan initialization data from the restart marker table entry corresponding to the
given MCU row index. Handles two operating modes based on the decode mode flags:
seekable mode (file-based) and streaming mode (buffer-based).

Algorithm:
  1. Calculate restart table entry offset: nMcuRowIndex * 0x28 (40 bytes per entry)
  2. Load restart marker table base pointer from pFrameInfo[0x120C]
  3. Copy bitstream state fields from restart table entry to pBitStream:
     - [+0x18] -> pBitStream[0]: Bit buffer contents
     - [+0x1C] -> pBitStream[1]: Bits remaining in buffer
     - [+0x20] -> pBitStream[3]: Additional state field
     - [+0x24] -> pBitStream[0x30]: Byte field (component index)
  4. Copy DC coefficient predictor values to pScanInfo:
     - [+0x04] -> pScanInfo[9]: DC predictor for component 0
     - [+0x08] -> pScanInfo[10]: DC predictor for component 1
     - [+0x0C] -> pScanInfo[11]: DC predictor for component 2
     - [+0x10] -> pScanInfo[12]: DC predictor for component 3
  5. Check decode mode at pFrameInfo[0]:
     - Seekable modes (2, 6, 0xE, 0x10, 0x12): Seek file and read new buffer
     - Streaming mode: Calculate buffer offset from current position

Parameters:
  nMcuRowIndex - Zero-based MCU row index to initialize from
  pBitStream   - Pointer to bitstream context structure (buffer, position, bit state)
  pScanInfo    - Pointer to scan info array (DC predictors at indices 9-12)
  pFrameInfo   - Pointer to frame info array (restart table at [0x120C], decode mode at [0])

Returns:
  0        - Success, bitstream positioned and DC predictors loaded
  -0x17    - Error: File seek failed (FUN_60018130 returned 0)
  -0x17    - Error: Buffer fill failed (FUN_60001050 returned non-zero)

Magic Numbers:
  0x28     - Size of each restart marker table entry (40 bytes)
  0x120C   - Frame info index for restart marker table pointer (4620 decimal)
  0x11     - Frame info index for stream base position (17 decimal)

Restart Table Entry Layout (40 bytes per MCU row):
  Offset   Size   Field
  0x00     4      File position / stream offset
  0x04     4      DC predictor component 0
  0x08     4      DC predictor component 1
  0x0C     4      DC predictor component 2
  0x10     4      DC predictor component 3
  0x18     4      Bit buffer contents
  0x1C     4      Bits remaining
  0x20     4      Additional state
  0x24     1      Component index byte

Decode Mode Values:
  2, 6, 0xE, 0x10, 0x12 - Seekable file modes (random access)
  Other                  - Streaming mode (sequential buffer)

functions.name: CopyJpegComponentData
functions.signature: void CopyJpegComponentData(int nComponentIndex, uint * pSourceComp, uint * pScanParams, int * pJpegContext)
functions.comment:
Copies JPEG component data from source structures to destination buffer slot.

Algorithm:
1. Calculate destination slot offset: nComponentIndex * 40 bytes (0x28)
2. Copy DCT parameters from pScanParams to dest buffer offsets 0x04-0x10
3. Copy coefficient data from pSourceComp to dest offsets 0x18-0x24
4. Read JPEG marker type from pJpegContext[0]
5. If progressive scan type (2,6,0xE,0x10,0x12): use pSourceComp[7]
6. Otherwise (baseline): use pSourceComp[4] for dest offset 0x00

Parameters:
  nComponentIndex - Zero-based component index (0-3 for Y,Cb,Cr,K channels)
  pSourceComp     - Component data with coefficients and quantization info
  pScanParams     - Scan parameters with DCT block dimensions
  pJpegContext    - Decoder context: [0]=marker type, [0x120C]=output buffer

Returns:
  void - Data copied directly to buffer at pJpegContext[0x120C]

Special Cases:
  SOF2(2), SOF6(6), SOF14(0xE), SOF16(0x10), SOF18(0x12) are progressive markers

functions.name: DecodeBaselineScanBlocks
functions.signature: int DecodeBaselineScanBlocks(uint pJpegContext, uint pScanState, int * pScanHeader)
functions.comment:
Decodes baseline (non-progressive) JPEG scan blocks using IDCT and Huffman decoding.

Algorithm:
1. Initialize component lookup tables (DC/AC Huffman tables, quantization tables)
2. Calculate total block count per MCU from scan header component data
3. Iterate over MCU rows (dwMcuRow) from pScanHeader[8] to context max rows
4. Iterate over MCU columns (dwMcuColumn) from pScanHeader[7] to context max cols
5. Call FUN_60004ff0 to prepare coefficient blocks for current MCU position
6. Apply 4x4 IDCT transform (g_pfnIdct4x4) to each block in the MCU
7. For each color component, apply dequantization (g_pfnDecodeProc21) and 
   output conversion (g_pfnDecodeProc18) to decoded coefficients
8. If restart interval hit (context+0x1c != 0), save position and return 1
9. After all MCUs processed, call finalization proc and return 0

Parameters:
  pJpegContext - Pointer to JPEG decoder context structure (passed as uint)
  pScanState   - Pointer to current scan state/buffer structure (passed as uint)
  pScanHeader  - Pointer to scan header with component info and MCU positions

Returns:
  0 - Scan completed successfully (all MCUs decoded)
  1 - Restart interval reached, caller should resume later

Magic Numbers:
  0x379c - Offset to sampling factor table in context
  0x37e0 - Offset to progressive mode flag in context
  0x36e4 - Offset to DC Huffman table pointer array
  0x36f4 - Offset to quantization table pointer array
  0x3704 - Offset to AC Huffman table pointer array
  0x37cc - Offset to component index lookup table
  0x4834 - Offset to coefficient block buffer pointer
  0x78   - Offset to MCU columns count
  0x7c   - Offset to MCU rows count
  0x80   - Size of one DCT coefficient block (128 bytes = 64 shorts)

Structure Layout (pScanHeader offsets):
  +0x00 - Component count in scan
  +0x1C - Current MCU column position
  +0x20 - Current MCU row position
  +0x24 - Output position array (per component)
  +0x34 - Component descriptor array pointer (stride 0x18)

functions.name: DecodeProgressiveScanBlocks
functions.signature: int DecodeProgressiveScanBlocks(void * pJpegContext, void * pScanState, int * pComponentInfo)
functions.comment:
Decodes JPEG progressive scan blocks for interleaved image data.
Processes MCU rows and columns iteratively, applying IDCT and dequantization.

Algorithm:
1. Initialize component block count arrays from scan parameters
2. Validate MCU row/column bounds against image dimensions
3. Call FUN_60004ff0 to set up decode parameters for current MCU
4. Apply IDCT 4x4 transform via g_pfnIdct4x4 for each block
5. Dequantize and decode blocks via g_pfnDecodeProc21/g_pfnDecodeProc18
6. Increment frame counter and check for restart marker interval
7. Process restart markers via FUN_6001be30 when interval reached
8. Reset component counters after restart marker
9. Update scan state position for next MCU row/column
10. Return 0 on completion, 1 on suspension, or error code

Parameters:
pJpegContext (void*): Pointer to JPEG decoder context structure
  - Offset 0x78: Image height in MCU rows
  - Offset 0x7C: Image width in MCU columns
  - Offset 0x37D0: Restart marker interval
  - Offset 0x37E0: Interleave mode flag
  - Offset 0x4834: Pointer to DCT coefficient buffer
pScanState (void*): Pointer to scan state tracking structure
  - Offset 0x24+: Per-component block counters array
  - Offset 0x34: Pointer to component descriptor array
pComponentInfo (int*): Component information array
  - Offset 0x00: Number of components in scan
  - Offset 0x18: Current frame counter
  - Offset 0x1C: Current MCU column position
  - Offset 0x20: Current MCU row position

Returns:
0: Scan completed successfully
1: Scan suspended (restart marker processing in progress)
Negative: Error code from restart marker handler (FUN_6001be30)

Special Cases:
- Handles restart marker intervals (RST0-RST7 markers: 0xD0-0xD7)
- Supports multiple components per scan (up to component count)
- Resets all component block counters after 8 restart intervals

Magic Numbers:
0x379C: Component scan parameter table offset in context
0x36E4, 0x36F4, 0x3704: Quantization table offsets
0x80: DCT block stride in bytes (8x8 block * 2 bytes per coefficient)
0x18: Component descriptor stride (24 bytes per component)

functions.name: ScaleQuantizationTable
functions.signature: void ScaleQuantizationTable(int nQuality, byte * pbSourceTable, ushort * pwDestTable)
functions.comment:
Scales a JPEG quantization table based on quality factor.

Converts a standard 64-element quantization table (8x8 DCT block) to scaled 16-bit values
based on the IJG libjpeg quality scaling algorithm.

Algorithm:
1. Compute scale factor based on quality:
   - quality < 1: scale = 5000 (minimum quality, max quantization)
   - quality 1-49: scale = 5000 / quality (inverse scaling)
   - quality 50-100: scale = 2 * (100 - quality) (linear scaling)
   - quality > 100: clamped to 100 (zero quantization)
2. For each of 64 table elements:
   a. Compute: scaledValue = (sourceValue * scaleFactor + 50) / 100
   b. Clamp result to range [1, 255]
   c. Store as 16-bit value in destination

Parameters:
  nQuality - JPEG quality factor (1-100 typical, higher = better quality)
  pbSourceTable - Pointer to 64-byte source quantization table
  pwDestTable - Pointer to 64-element ushort destination array

Returns:
  void

Magic Numbers:
  5000 - Maximum scale factor for lowest quality
  0x32 (50) - Rounding offset for division by 100
  0x40 (64) - DCT block size (8x8)
  0xff (255) - Maximum quantization value
  0x64 (100) - Division constant and quality threshold

Called By:
  InitializeQuantizationAndHuffmanTables - During JPEG encoder initialization

functions.name: BuildHuffmanTable
functions.signature: void BuildHuffmanTable(byte * pbBitCounts, byte * pbSymbolValues, int * pnHuffmanTable)
functions.comment:
Builds a Huffman decoding table from bit counts and symbol values.

Algorithm:
1. Initialize the Huffman table arrays to zero (256 entries each)
2. For each bit length 1-16, read count from pbBitCounts and fill anBitLengthPerSymbol array
3. Generate canonical Huffman codes - same bit length symbols get sequential codes
4. Populate output table with code values and bit lengths indexed by symbol

Parameters:
  pbBitCounts - Pointer to 16-byte array of symbol counts per bit length (1-16 bits)
  pbSymbolValues - Pointer to symbol value array (indices 0 to nTotalSymbols-1)
  pnHuffmanTable - Pointer to output Huffman table structure:
                   +0x008: int[256] - Bit lengths indexed by symbol
                   +0x408: short[256] - Code values indexed by symbol

Returns:
  void

Structure Layout:
  Offset   Size   Field              Description
  0x008    1024   nBitLengths[256]   Bit length for each symbol (4 bytes each)
  0x408    512    wCodes[256]        Huffman code for each symbol (2 bytes each)

Magic Numbers:
  0x100 (256) - Maximum number of symbols in table
  0x11 (17) - Loop bound for bit lengths 1-16
  0x408 - Offset to code values array in output table
  0x808 - Stack allocation for two 257-entry int arrays
